title: Learning an Efficient Multi-Turn Dialogue Evaluator from Multiple LLM Judges

bias_targets.methodology: Mitigated during data annotation by selecting LLM judges that are completely distinct from the models used to generate the dialogue responses, preventing evaluators from unfairly rating their own outputs higher.
Evaluated and eliminated by swapping the A/B order of each dialogue pair during pairwise comparison, retaining only those samples where all judges provided consistent outputs regardless of the order.
Controlled during the dataset curation phase by explicitly filtering response pairs to ensure that the difference in word length between the competing responses did not exceed 10 words.

Addressed by constructing a pairwise preference dataset rather than relying on direct scoring, and training a lightweight evaluator using maximum likelihood estimation to aggregate preferences from multiple judges.

Mitigated by learning a unified evaluator model from the collective preference knowledge of multiple advanced LLM judges, reducing the variance and instability typical of single-judge prompt responses.
